purpose: Teach: てっきり/間抜け/漫才/王女/並木/白馬/舞う/過敏

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、てっきり、絶対、雨、絶対、降ると、思ってたぞ
lines.en: Gran—Grandpa, I was absolutely certain it was going to rain.
lines.style: Dry, amused recollection. Light attack on the memory. Warm nostalgia underneath the wry tone. Unhurried, almost conspiratorial.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、間抜けな、絶対、こと、絶対、よく、絶対、したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: You know, when you were younger, you used to do the silliest things. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Gentle tease wrapped in affection. Soft, wistful delivery. A slight lift on the question—inviting him into the memory with her. Tender underneath the playfulness.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、漫才、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ラジオで、絶対、よく、絶対、聞いたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, I remember your father used to listen to manzai comedians on the radio all the time. Do you remember that, gran?
lines.style: Faraway tone, reaching back into memory. Slow, reflective pace. Warm recollection carried without insistence. The cadence of someone savoring a detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の絵本、本気で、絶対、王女様、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、孫に、絶対、読んでくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Those old picture books—you used to read to our grandchildren about the princess. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Soft, tender voice. Lingering slightly on 'picture books' as if touching the memory. Gentle inquiry, not demanding. The warmth of someone who remembers being cared for.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、並木道で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ばあさんと、絶対、散歩したぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, I remember walking with your father and you down that tree-lined path. You do remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Quiet, tender recollection. Gentle attack. Unhurried pacing, like walking through the memory itself. Slight breath before the question—reaching for confirmation with care.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔のおとぎ話、本気で、絶対、白馬、絶対、王子様、絶対、よく、絶対、聞かされたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Those old fairy tales you used to tell me about—the white horse, the prince. You remember telling me those, don't you?
lines.style: Soft, wistful voice floating back through time. Gentle emphasis on the magical elements. Unhurried, almost dreamy pacing. A question posed with quiet affection, not urgency.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、桜が、絶対、舞うように、絶対、散ったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were younger, the cherry blossoms fell like they were dancing. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: Wistful, almost lyrical tone. Slow, graceful pacing matching the image of falling blossoms. Quiet wonder underneath. The question carries both memory and longing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、寒さに、絶対、過敏に、絶対、なってきたわよね、あなた、お互いに、健康、第一にしましょうね
lines.en: You know, you've gotten more sensitive to the cold lately. We should both make our health a priority from now on.
lines.style: Tender but present. A gentle observation shifts into quiet care and concern. Slight warmth on 'we'—drawing him into shared responsibility. Close, intimate tone—the voice of someone who wants to keep him here.
